statement: Mwari (Mwali) is a high-god oracular tradition centered on the Matopo/Matobo Hills, principal historical shrine at Njelele (also Matonjeni; Shona Mabweadziva, "place of spring waters"), with a broader network of subsidiary shrines. The god's voice is delivered through mediums from within cave shrines; historically served both Shona/Kalanga and, after Ndebele settlement in the 1830s-40s, Ndebele consultors, especially for rainmaking and political counsel. M.L. Daneel, The God of the Matopo Hills: An Essay on the Mwari Cult in Rhodesia (Mouton, 1970), based on 1965-67 fieldwork, is the foundational modern academic study.

sources.citation: Daneel, M.L. The God of the Matopo Hills: An Essay on the Mwari Cult in Rhodesia. The Hague: Mouton, 1970.
